data.text: Live probe 2026-10-30 00:26 SAST against Always On (runtime hearth_h1_recovered_20260908_v1, code pinned at 5451423, not this checkout): /health ok; /time ok; /config 113 keys, no secret-bearing keys exposed; /where points at the runtime's own storage. /query requires {text}; 200 in 0.65 s with answer, 17 to 19 citations, full trace (confidence, coverage, selection, budgets, latency, transitional_complexity, tc_routing), and cognitive_episode_write_ok and lived_memory_write_ok both true, so every probe is now an episode in Rick's live stores (three queries written by this verification). Finding: selection.shards was empty on both queries; the merged shortlist was 13 cognitive episodes plus 4 ANN, CELF accepted 0, reads_used 17 against reads_limit 5, and the rendered answer is a chain of references to earlier Q/A episodes rather than corpus text. Serving works; the answer path is dominated by memory recall. That belongs to the cognitive and OrthoRoute cards (WB-0018, WB-0021), noted here because this is where it was seen.

Control probe, budget_reads=20: 4 document shards selected (spec, roadmap, diary), CELF accepted 4, 15 memory items, one lived-memory citation; 0.87 s. So the corpus path works; at the default budget of 5 the memory layer alone uses 17 reads and no shard is ever considered. The answer head quoted the previous probe's question verbatim: each query becomes an episode the next query recalls.

Seen during WB-0025 (2026-10-30): on the live runtime, cognitive recall (k=12, unlimited token and slot budget) fills the shortlist before any corpus shard at the default read budget of 5; reads_used 17 against a limit of 5, shards empty, CELF accepted 0. With budget_reads=20 shards appear. Also: every /query writes an episode, and the next /query recalls it first, so repeated questions feed on their own echoes. Verify whether memory reads should count against the read budget, and whether a query's own fresh episode should be excluded from immediate recall.

Seen during WB-0025 (2026-10-30): CELF coverage accepted 0 of the shortlist at default settings because the shortlist held no corpus shards (memory crowded them out); with budget_reads=20 it accepted 4 of 17 pops. The selector itself behaved; its input did not. See WB-0018.

Seen during WB-0025 (2026-10-30): tests/test_lived_memory.py::test_reopened_read_operations_are_database_hash_stable failed once inside a 65-file run (expected and actual database hashes differed) and passed twice in isolation. Order- or state-dependent; the suite shares the tracked storage tree. Check whether the test uses the repository store instead of a temporary one.

Finding: scripts/verify_mcp.py returns FAIL with only error_type ExceptionGroup, and the reason, reproduced step by step, is its own security check: on the login runtime fram://config includes api_key with a non-empty value (masked de...ey, almost certainly a dev placeholder, but present), while REST /config omits it. So: the script fails closed correctly; its output hides why (the ExceptionGroup wrapper swallows the RuntimeError message, which was written not to echo bodies, but the message itself is safe to print). Verdict: works, yes; works well, no, on the runtime: a config secret field is served over MCP until the runtime is moved to a commit at or after e5a4ddc, and the verify script should name its own check failures. Finished; the runtime upgrade is Rick's decision (WB-0026 ops / Always On).

From WB-0012: the Always On runtime is pinned at 5451423, which predates e5a4ddc (MCP fram://config api_key redaction). Moving the runtime forward is a decision; the memory note fram-always-on says how the runtime is pinned.
